required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh (M,) int64 output inside run().

One logical traversal of each row by the program that owns it, in column chunks, keeping a running (best value, best index) pair; chunk max/argmax with lowest-index ties, merged so that the earliest column wins ties (a strict greater-than test when chunks are visited in increasing order); -inf padding for columns beyond N; no partial results in global memory; the final index is stored once.

forbidden_substitutions.message: A library argmax/max/topk/sort replaces the whole computation.
A tensor-method argmax/max on the host replaces the kernel reduction.
A non-strict merge (with chunks in increasing order) or right-tie-break would pick a later occurrence; first occurrence is required.
Atomic merging of partial results across programs is not the single-program-per-row structure.
Only the (M,) int64 output is expected; a second buffer suggests scratch for partial results.
A transpose copy inside run() is only acceptable on a dim != 1 path that the benchmark never takes.

required_evidence.message: No -inf fill/identity found; out-of-range columns must never win.
No int64 index handling found; the output must be int64.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (M,) int64 tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with x

timing_boundary.notes: Measured: GPU time of all device work run() causes (the row-scan kernel); the no-op contiguity guard, the output allocation call and chunk-count arithmetic are host work, not GPU time. For the benchmark (dim == 1, contiguous x) no copy or transpose may occur; nothing is cached across calls.
